flow.costPlain: Running Intuit's cloud services and customer support ($894M), product costs ($16M), and amortization of acquired technology ($43M).

opex.name: Selling and marketing
opex.note: Selling TurboTax, QuickBooks and Credit Karma — spending continues through the quiet season to win customers before tax time.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma and Mailchimp — increasingly, AI agents that do bookkeeping and tax prep.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Amortization of other acquired intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of customer relationships and other assets from acquisitions like Mailchimp and Credit Karma.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: A charge to reshape the company — severance and related costs, versus just $1M a year ago.

follow100Note: Q4 is Intuit's seasonal trough — the same company keeps far more of each $100 in tax season. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Intuit doesn't present a gross-profit subtotal; the cost line combines its three reported cost-of-revenue lines. Segment revenue: Consumer is stated in the release; Global Business Solutions is the remainder of total revenue.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: Q4 is the seasonal low point

oneTimers: A $293M restructuring charge (versus $1M a year ago) is the quarter's big distortion — and share-based compensation added another $507M of cost that GAAP counts.
Tax swung the comparison: a $177M provision this year versus a $15M benefit a year ago. That swing, plus restructuring, is why net income fell even though operating income rose 40%.
With this release Intuit guided FY27: revenue of $23,279M–$23,512M (+9–10%) and GAAP EPS of $20.12–$20.36; it also raised the dividend 15% to $1.38 after buying back $5.5B of stock in FY26.
otherDetail: Interest and other income, net of $135M, less $70M of interest expense, added $65M.
pngFooterNote: Cost combines Intuit's three reported cost-of-revenue lines.

segments.name: Global Business Solutions
segments.note: QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small and mid-sized businesses. The online ecosystem brought in $2,600M (+17%), with QuickBooks Online accounting revenue up 20% — this segment pays the bills while tax season sleeps.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: TurboTax ($153M — a trickle in the off-season), Credit Karma ($743M, +16% — the quarter's engine) and ProTax for professional preparers ($34M).

takeaways.text: This 'quiet' quarter closed Intuit's first $20B-plus year: FY26 revenue of $21,448M rose 14%, with its 'Big Bets' — AI-driven expert and money products — growing 34% to 30% of revenue.
takeaways.title: A record year, finished quietly

takeaways.text: QuickBooks Online accounting revenue grew 20% in the quarter and Credit Karma 16% to $743M. The always-on businesses now dwarf off-season TurboTax ($153M) — Intuit is far less of a one-season company than it used to be.
takeaways.title: QuickBooks and Credit Karma did the work

takeaways.text: A $293M restructuring charge and a tax swing cut net income 5% to $363M despite operating income rising 40% to $475M. Read the quarter on revenue, not on the bottom line.
takeaways.title: Charges and tax hid a stronger quarter

verdict: Intuit's seasonally quiet quarter still grew revenue 14% to $4.4B — QuickBooks and Credit Karma did the work while TurboTax sleeps — but a $293M restructuring charge and a tax swing cut net profit 5% to $363M.
